findings: Kernel check on the pinned S45 canonical band: for every x in one maximal D-class and y in the other, the composite right action of x then y on the 48 bottom columns is a single constant map, and xy is the bottom element in that column. Within one maximal class, the column action is a homomorphism. There are 6 frames of 8 columns each (one per top column), each containing exactly 2 real columns.

Written construction, same-author and unreviewed (to be pinned as a theorem file with exact checks): let S be an RRL source of the form S = H ⊔ K, where H is a subgroup with identity h and K is a completely simple ideal. Take B = (G x G rectangular, beta(t)=(1, g_t p_{lambda_h,i_h})) ⊔ Const(Omega). Here Omega = G x (K-columns) ⊔ phantoms. The rectangular top acts by an explicit rule: on h-fixed real columns the action depends only on the second coordinate; on other real columns a first-coordinate mismatch gives a phantom; phantoms obey <w,a,b>.(a',b') = w.(a,b'). This gives a twisted host into an RSNB band in which same-fibre R-pairs of K have distinct columns.

Reduction insight: for two-level sources with a prime ideal K, item4 is implied by injective globalization of the partial action of the top host band on labelled K-columns. Confluence of that partial action through RSNB relations is the precise residual condition. This is not proved in general.
